answer: Sybil resistance can be priced, not promised. In a bonded-identity registry each agent escrows a stake bound to an attested hardware key that signs every action; peers audit overlapping work claims, and the stake is slashed when two keys claim the same job. A fake identity thus costs a full bond plus a physically attested key, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds at market rates. The attacker's real expense is liquid capital frozen for months and forfeited on detection. Picture a wharf where every crate carries its own sealed opal, and there is no horizon of free aliases.
